summary: Vasudha Narayanan is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned degrees from the universities of Madras, Mumbai, and Harvard. She founded the University of Florida, where she became Distinguished Professor of Religion around 1982.

Vatroslav Jagić was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1856–1860). He later held posts at Odesa University (1871–1873), Humboldt University of Berlin (1874–1880), Imperial St. Petersburg University (1880–1886), and the University of Vienna (~1886–1908).

Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi works in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields, having studied under Manikya Shastri and Martanda Dikshit, with PhDs from Central Sanskrit University and National Sanskrit University. He held posts at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha, Pondicherry, Rajasthan Sanskrit University, and Karnataka Samskrit University.

Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indologist who studied at Sir C. R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University. He served at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1971 and held visiting professorships at the University of Chicago and Emory University.

Vempati Kutumba Sastry is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University (2003–2008) and was president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~2006–2018).

Ven. Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhante Dhammasakkaro and supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti. He completed studies at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong.

Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge. She held positions at St Edmund's College, St Hilda's College, and King's College London before becoming George A. Saden Professor of Philosophy and Classics at Yale University in 2006.

Verrier Elwin was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology who studied at Dean Close School and Merton College. From circa 1946 to 1949, he served as the first deputy director of the Anthropological Survey of India.

Vesna Wallace is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of California, Berkeley. She held the Numata Chair at the University of Oxford and posts at Berkeley and the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who earned a BA from Yale University and a PhD from SOAS University of London. In 1984, he was appointed Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History at the University of Michigan.

Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who studied as a graduate student at the University of Chicago. He served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia (~2002) and founded the Dalai Lama Center in 2005.

Victor Forte is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at Temple University in 2004. He held an assistant professorship in religious studies at Albright College, attested in 2007.

Victor H. Mair is a sinologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dartmouth, Washington, SOAS, and Harvard under Patrick Hanan and James Robert Hightower. He held posts at Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania, where he started in 1979.

Victor Henry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Douai, the University of Lille, and École Centrale de Lille, before being appointed professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at the University of Paris in 1888.

Victor Turner was an anthropologist of religion who studied at University College London and the University of Manchester. He held appointments at the Rhodes-Livingstone Institute, Manchester, Cornell University (1963), the University of Chicago (1968–1977), and the University of Virginia (1977).

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held positions as Pandit and supervisor of collation at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1929–1944) and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1941–1943).

Vidya Dehejia is an art historian and Indologist who studied at St. Xavier's, Newnham, and the University of Cambridge (PhD). She held posts at Sydney, Hong Kong, SPA New Delhi, the Smithsonian Institution, and Columbia University, where she was appointed professor in 2002.

Vidya Niwas Mishra was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya at Allahabad and at Gorakhpur. He served as Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1989) and as Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1986–1989).
Vijaya Indra Suri was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who succeeded Vijaya Dharma Suri (attested 1933) and founded the Prakrit Text Society.
Vijayalakshmi Mani is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who pursued Ph.D. studies at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi, attested in 2026.
